limitations: Wasm buffer length is allocated linear-memory length, not live native or managed allocation, allocator free space, process RSS, or a memory-leak measurement.
Remaining configured growth is the difference from the statically decoded 2 GiB maximum. It is not guaranteed allocatable headroom.
Each artifact was measured once, in separate processes. This is a capacity observation, not a statistical timing or FPS benchmark.

Bodies, URLs, byte counts and gesture totals match, but immediate replay blocks service workers and changes original network/cache timing. Baseline and candidate request sequences differ at 48 of 170 positions; each differs at 46 positions from the original capture.
Wheel event chunking and actual frame counts differ. The same public camera/data-ready/pause/resume checkpoints completed; this is not a frame-by-frame identical execution.

Two baseline first-gesture wheel records arrive at Node after the CDP command acknowledgment but before the camera checkpoint. These are asynchronous observation receipt times; the full delivered delta is retained.

Grow/resize hooks stream scalar records through a binding independent of periodic sampling, and recorded growth during timed-out polls. Timestamps are Node receipt times and may be delayed; abrupt browser termination could lose pending records.
Bounded observation calls timed out in both runs. Every recorded error and affected timestamp is retained; successful protocol completion does not imply continuously responsive UI.
Neither replay reproduced the original live native allocation abort. Passing this finite corpus and three cycles does not prove all live tile sets or future interactions are safe.
